mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate indicates easy monetary policy, which may stimulate investment and increase S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher when FEDFUNDS is low.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand, which may boost economic growth and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not higher when housing starts increase.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment rate suggests a strong labor market, which may positively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher when unemployment is low.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production indicates economic expansion, which may increase S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not higher when industrial production rises.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rate above 0.15% may signal tightening, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not negative when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.15%.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth slows but inflation rises, stagflation may occur, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth decelerates while CPIAUCSL increases
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not negative during stagflation.

mechanism_narrative: High retail sales in late-cycle expansion may not prevent an economic slowdown, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative when retail sales are high in late-cycle.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment with increasing unemployment suggests conflicting labor trends, potentially causing market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative when employment and unemployment both rise.
